Comments: No primary-source URL found in this run for an operational tax e-filing/e-service portal with online payments; only secondary/social posts were surfaced, so scored unknown (searched for "BURS e-services portal" and "Botswana efiling BURS").

revision_notes: Row was routed as fast-path (score 0, no source) but a single light Exa search immediately surfaced an authoritative primary source: the official BURS e-Services portal (eservices.burs.org.bw), whose published Terms and Conditions confirm it handles taxpayer registration, submission/processing of tax returns, and (clause 24) cooperation with banks to enable users to pay monies due to the Commissioner General electronically. This directly contradicts the Unknown score, so the row was moved to the full path and rescored to 4=Yes. Not confirmed as linked specifically to the BISS/BACH instant payment rail (payments are bank-mediated), which is noted as a limitation.
revised_comments: The Botswana Unified Revenue Service (BURS) operates an official e-Services web portal (eservices.burs.org.bw) through which taxpayers register, file tax returns, and process payments. Under the portal's terms of use, BURS cooperates with banks to enable users to pay monies due under Botswana's revenue laws electronically. This constitutes an operational government tax e-filing and e-payment portal, though online payments are executed via partner banks rather than a dedicated instant-payment rail.

Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: No primary evidence found in this run for broad person-to-government digital payments (e.g., online tax payment portal allowing payment), beyond general statements about planned digitisation of government revenue collection; therefore scored limited/unknown pending better evidence (searched for "BURS pay taxes online", "Botswana pay tax online portal").
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Light check surfaced a partially authoritative picture rather than a clean Unknown, so moved to full path. BURS's own payments page confirms digital-adjacent channels already in use for specific tax types (point-of-sale for VAT, direct debit for large Income Tax payers) alongside the e-Services portal enabling bank-mediated e-payment; a July 2025 Mmegi report on the Bank of Botswana's "Digital BoB2024" initiative confirms broader government revenue digitisation was still targeted for Q2 2025 and not yet comprehensive. Evidence supports Limited Use (2) rather than Unknown or No, but stops short of Active Use given fees/fines/utility payments are not evidenced as digitised.
revised_comments: Citizens and businesses in Botswana can already make some government payments digitally: VAT is payable by point-of-sale card payment, large Income Tax payers may pay by direct debit, and the BURS e-Services portal supports bank-mediated electronic payment of amounts due under the revenue laws. A broader national initiative (Digital BoB2024) to route government revenue collection directly through digital platforms has been rolled out from around mid-2025, but comprehensive digital payment of the full range of government fees, licences, fines and utility bills is not yet evidenced, indicating limited rather than fully active use of digital P2G payments.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: No primary legal text or regulator directive was found confirming mandatory breach notification requirements in force; search results referenced a 2024 Data Protection Act with 72-hour notification but primary act text was not located in sources gathered in this run, so scored unknown (searched "Botswana data breach notification requirement", "Data Protection Act 2024 Botswana breach notification").
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Light check immediately surfaced an authoritative, directly on-point source (DLA Piper's Data Protection Laws of the World, Botswana breach notification page), confirmed against Botswana's consolidated Data Protection Act (No. 32 of 2018, sections 33-34, botswanalaws.com) requiring data controllers to notify the Commissioner without delay and within 72 hours where feasible. A further authoritative source, the new Cybersecurity Act (No. 21 of 2025, BOCRA), imposes mandatory incident reporting (within 8 hours) for critical information infrastructure operators. Row moved to full path and rescored from Unknown to Mandatory (3); the original note's uncertainty about locating primary text is resolved.
revised_comments: Botswana's Data Protection Act, 2018 (Act No. 32 of 2018) requires a data controller to notify the Information and Data Protection Commissioner of a personal data breach without delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, unless the breach is unlikely to pose a risk to data subjects' rights and freedoms; data processors must notify controllers without undue delay. The Cybersecurity Act, 2025 additionally imposes mandatory, shorter (8-hour) incident reporting obligations on operators of critical information infrastructure, including financial and payment infrastructure. Payment data breach notification in Botswana is therefore mandatory rather than discretionary.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: No publicly accessible scheme rulebooks for BISS/BACH were found on the Bank of Botswana website; only descriptive pages and oversight/recognition policy documents were located (searched "BISS rulebook", "BACH rules", and Bank of Botswana payments pages; found BISS description and oversight policies but not rulebooks) ([Bank of Botswana – BISS](https://www.bankofbotswana.bw/content/botswana-interbank-settlement-system)).
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The originally cited BISS description page was re-verified and confirmed genuine but does not itself contain scheme rules. Further searches located the primary legal basis: the National Clearance and Settlement Systems Act, 2003, section 5, requires the constitution and rules of every recognised clearance/settlement system (which includes BISS and BACH, per the 2019 National Payments System Oversight Policy) to be kept at the Bank of Botswana's offices and the operator's Botswana head office, open for public inspection during normal office hours; the 2005 NCSS Regulations (reg. 12(e), reg. 13-15) require management bodies to lodge their constitution, rules, procedures and service level agreements with the Bank. No evidence was found that the rules themselves are published online as downloadable documents (the Bank's website publishes the Act, Regulations and Oversight Policy, but not the BISS/BACH rulebooks). This supports 'Partial - On Request' (2) rather than Unknown or Fully Public.
revised_comments: Botswana's National Clearance and Settlement Systems Act, 2003 and its 2005 Regulations require that the constitution and rules governing any recognised clearance and settlement system, including the Botswana Interbank Settlement System (BISS) and Botswana Automated Clearing House (BACH), be lodged with the Bank of Botswana and kept open for public inspection at the operator's head office during normal business hours. The Bank publishes the underlying legislation, regulations and its National Payments System Oversight Policy on its website, but the scheme rulebooks themselves are not published online as downloadable documents, making them accessible on request/inspection rather than fully public.

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: No credible quantified estimate was found in this run for the share of government payments digitized. Evidence indicates a project to digitise government revenue collection with launch target (Q2 2025), but not an overall adoption percentage; thus scored unknown.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Light check surfaced substantial credible evidence of existing G2P digitisation programmes, so moved to full path: the Bank of Botswana's NPSS 2020-2024 report describes an existing prepaid card scheme for unbanked beneficiaries and an Electronic Coupon System for social grants; a May 2025 Biometric Update article confirms the SmartSwitch biometric card system disburses food-grant payments to over 75,000 beneficiaries; a BotswanaPost/Software Group case study describes a Digital Post Office platform disbursing pensions to over 115,000 retired government employees with millions of monthly wallet transactions; and the Global Digital Identity Index govtech profile records that active public-employee pension contribution records have been fully digitised since 2017, though the share of pension benefits paid digitally to individual accounts is not disclosed. None of these sources provides a consolidated percentage of total government payments (by value or volume) made digitally versus cash/cheque, which the variable's scale strictly requires. Given the variable needs a percentage bucket and no authoritative aggregate figure exists, the score is kept at 0 rather than guessed, but flagged for human review because the qualitative evidence clearly indicates non-trivial digitisation is already under way and a specialist may be able to locate or estimate an aggregate figure.
revised_comments: The Government of Botswana disburses a substantial share of social transfers and pensions through digital channels. The SmartSwitch biometric card system, in use since 2006, serves over 75,000 food-grant beneficiaries with biometrically authenticated digital payments, and the BotswanaPost Digital Post Office platform disburses pensions to more than 115,000 retired government employees alongside agency banking and mobile wallet services. Active public-sector employee pension contribution records have been fully digitised since 2017. A consolidated, government-wide percentage figure for the share of all G2P payments made digitally rather than by cash or cheque is not publicly available.

Definition: Whether refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons, migrants, and stateless persons can legally access and open digital payment accounts, and practical barriers or enablers for these populations.
Comments: No credible evidence found in this run for refugee/migrant access to digital payments (e.g., KYC exceptions, UNHCR payment programmes in Botswana). Searched "Botswana refugee mobile money", "UNHCR Botswana cash assistance digital payments", "KYC refugee Botswana".
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Light check surfaced substantive, mostly authoritative material contradicting a clean Unknown, so moved to full path. The AfricanLII Botswana Refugee Law Reader (updated 2025) states plainly that national law makes no specific provision for refugees and asylum-seekers to access financial inclusion/bank accounts. A UN Botswana news item confirms UNHCR, with government cooperation, runs a Cash-Based Intervention disbursing cash assistance via BotswanaPost at Dukwi refugee camp. A Botswana Gazette report (April 2025) confirms UNHCR worked with BOCRA and mobile operators to restore mobile network (and by extension mobile-money-enabling) access for refugees affected by mandatory SIM re-registration, after many were disconnected for lacking national ID. A further Gazette report (Aug 2024) on the Refugees (Recognition and Management) Bill notes that formal refugee ID issuance to enable KYC compliance is pending Section 25 becoming operational. Evidence supports Partial (2): practical/ad hoc access exists via humanitarian and regulatory interventions, but no general legal right to open standard payment accounts exists yet.
revised_comments: Botswana's national law currently makes no specific general provision for refugees, asylum-seekers or stateless persons to open standard bank or digital payment accounts. In practice, access is partial and largely dependent on ad hoc humanitarian and regulatory arrangements: UNHCR, in cooperation with the government, disburses cash assistance to refugees at Dukwi camp through BotswanaPost's digital payment infrastructure, and UNHCR has worked with the telecoms regulator and mobile network operators to restore mobile network access (a precondition for mobile money) for refugees affected by mandatory SIM registration requirements. The Refugees (Recognition and Management) Act, 2024 provides for refugee identity documents intended to facilitate future KYC compliance, but this provision was not yet fully operational as of the latest reporting.
